governance.note: One structural lever on top of miso23 (all miso23/miso22/miso21 levers retained byte-for-byte). Replace the PJM import seam's synthetic gas x HR x load-shape reference price with measured PJM-west border-hub hourly DA LMP (equal-weight mean of CHICAGO GEN, AEP GEN, ATSI GEN hubs from PJM Data Miner). GROUNDING: the synthetic formula produces a flat/high import offer that under-imports in 2024/2025 (keeper gmModel import 17.0/5.8 TWh vs actual 23.1/19.0); the measured PJM LMP IS the actual border price and passes the forward-admissibility test (rule #13: the same quantity could be produced from a forward PJM price forecast, and it responds to changed conditions). Implementation mirrors the proven CAISO intertie-hub pattern: loader reads pjm_border_lmp_hourly_MISO.parquet (curated from PJM Data Miner CSVs, EPT->Central conversion, dense 8760-hour schema), injector overwrites ONLY the PJM seam import/export rows with measured_price +/- hurdle AFTER inject_reference_price_mc (so SPP/South seams keep their gas x HR pricing). All 8 import tranches get the same measured price (the PJM border LMP IS the marginal cost regardless of flow volume). NO firm floor, NO adder, NO haircut -- pure measured-price mechanism. Gated on miso_pjm_lmp_import_pricing=True; other ISOs unaffected. NOT residual-fitted: this is measured-data substitution for a synthetic estimate, grounded in rule #11 (prefer accurate/measured data over estimates).

model_miss_notes: The exceptions ledger is EMPTY by design: every out-of-tolerance criterion is a genuine MODEL MISS to fix in a later lever. (1) CC_REGULAR OVER-RUN: gmModel CC_REGULAR +20.5/+19.5/+13.0 TWh vs EIA-923 (2023/24/25). The measured PJM LMP mechanism reduced CC by -3.4/-5.1/-4.3 TWh vs keeper (right direction), but the over-run persists. This is NOT offer-curve-addressable (CC excess is in its measured-flat econ body) and NOT import-addressable beyond what the measured price already provides. Root cause: missing scarcity mechanism (reserve-demand co-optimization) that would price up CT/ST_GAS hours and pull CC down. (2) CT_PEAKER UNDER-RUN: gmModel CT_PEAKER -18.2/-15.1/-16.6 TWh (2023/24/25). Essentially unchanged by this lever (+1.4/-0.4/+0.1 vs keeper). Gated by the missing scarcity/ELMP mechanism (DATA-BLOCKED, not part of this work). (3) IMPORT LEVEL: the measured PJM LMP fixed 2025 import under-run (21.4 vs 19.0 actual, was 5.8 keeper) but OVER-imports in 2023 (46.7 vs 37.9) and 2024 (32.4 vs 23.1). The 2023/2024 overshot is because measured PJM LMP ($28-29/MWh mean) is cheaper than the model's internal MISO clearing price, so the LP dispatches the full import capacity. This is the CORRECT price-responsive mechanism; the overshot signals the model's internal MISO price is too high relative to PJM (likely the CC over-run inflating domestic supply cost), which is the CC/CT substitution root cause, not the import mechanism. (4) COAL_BIT UNDER-RUN: -8.9/-7.8/-6.5 TWh (2023/24/25), slightly improved vs keeper. (5) CO2 UNDER-RUN 2023/2024: -8.3%/-8.3%, consistent with thermal displacement by imports. (6) STORAGE THROUGHPUT 2025: +1436% (carried over from keeper). (7) PRICE TAIL (C3c): 0 model >$200 hours vs 30/37/88 actual -- scarcity/RDT not modeled. Prices PASS C3a (avg within tol). Dispatch correlation PASSES C4 (gas r=0.87-0.92, coal r=0.94-0.95). Determination: NOT-YET, decided by C1 hard gate (CC/CT substitution). This run IS structurally more faithful (measured price > synthetic estimate, rule #11) and is a keeper candidate on those grounds even though 2023/2024 imports overshot.
